data.value: Windows moves files as needed and keeps your data, but any resize carries risk: make sure important files are backed up and do not power off during the operation. Continue?

data.name: Resize_ShrinkAndCreateConfirmBody
data.value: The partition is shrunk first; if that succeeds, a new partition is created and formatted in the freed space. Windows moves files as needed and keeps your data, but any resize carries risk: make sure important files are backed up and do not power off during the operation. Continue?

data.name: Resize_ShrinkAndCreateDone
data.value: Done: the partition is now {0} and a new partition was created in the freed space.

data.name: Destructive_FormatExplanation
data.value: Erases the file system on this partition and writes a new, empty one. The partition itself, its size and its drive letter stay. Choose NTFS if you want to be able to shrink or extend it later.

data.name: Destructive_DeleteExplanation
data.value: Removes the partition from the partition table. The space becomes unallocated and can be used for new partitions. Files are not wiped, but they are no longer reachable without recovery tools.

data.name: Destructive_Deleted
data.value: Done: the partition was deleted and its space is unallocated.

data.name: ShrinkAnalysis_Subtitle
data.value: Finds the files Windows refuses to move and shows how far this volume can really shrink. Read-only: nothing is changed.

data.name: ShrinkAnalysis_TargetTip
data.value: Volume size you would like to reach, e.g. 300GB. Leave empty for used data + 10 %.
